# Preface {.unnumbered}

On January 5, 2025, the MTA began tolling vehicles entering Manhattan's Congestion Relief Zone (CRZ). This report estimates the causal effect of that policy on subway ridership and related outcomes, using a pre-registered design and several estimators applied to the same panels.

The analysis is organized around four research questions (RQ1-RQ4) stated in the [analysis plan](../config/analysis_plan.md) before any post-treatment causal estimates were produced. The plan text is frozen; amendments appear only in its Deviations Log.

## How to read this report

| Chapter | Contents |
|---|---|
| [Background](01-background.qmd) | Policy setting, timeline, questions, and hypotheses |
| [Data](02-data.qmd) | Sources, zone assignment, panels, and sample windows |
| [Methods](03-methods.qmd) | Estimators S1-S6, robustness checks, threats to validity |
| [Results](04-results.qmd) | Primary estimates by outcome and specification |
| [Comparison](05-comparison.qmd) | Cross-estimator disagreement (RQ4) |
| [Discussion](06-discussion.qmd) | Interpretation, benchmarks, and limitations |

All figures and tables that report causal estimates are rendered from serialized outputs in `results/estimates/` and `results/figures/`. Quarto chapters do not re-fit estimators.

## Reproducibility

```bash
make data       # public ingest (Socrata, NOAA, CRZ geofence)
make panel      # build panels + invariant tests
make estimates  # estimator × outcome × spec grid
make report     # render this book
```

Treatment definitions, distance bands, and sample windows live in `config/treatment.yaml`. Panel provenance (row counts, content hashes, exclusions) is recorded in `data/processed/manifest.json`.
